questions.question: Orient found two unmet prerequisites in BK-394's dossier: BK-398 (round-trip clauses, open, S, no decision left) and ID-244 (seeding hook, open decision). Which scope should this PR take?

options.label: BK-394 + BK-398, registry untouched (Recommended)
options.description: All of BK-394 items 2 and 4-7, with BK-398's three clause amendments co-shipped, since Memory's folding makes them false for Memory too. The conformance registry stays as is (MemoryBackend is still a Backend via DriverBackend), so ID-244 is not triggered. Dafny DeleteFolder gets the carve-out only; encoding wiring stays with BK-434. One large PR.

options.label: Split: Memory + ADRs now, guide later
options.description: This PR: Memory drivers, spec amendments, BK-398, ADR-0042/RFC-0017/new ADR accepted, kernel exported. Item 5 (custom-backend guide rewrite, check script, homepage snippet, migration section) goes to a follow-up item. Smaller review loop, but ADR-0042 is accepted while the documented route is still Backend subclassing for a while.

options.label: BK-398 first, as its own PR
options.description: Ship BK-398 alone (docs only, S) to honour the dossier's stated order, then run BK-394 as framed. Two loops; the first is cheap but adds a merge before any BK-394 work lands.

questions.question: Orient found two unmet prerequisites in BK-394's dossier: BK-398 (round-trip clauses, open, S, no decision left) and ID-244 (seeding hook, open decision). Which scope should this PR take?
Where should the kernel's new public names live (Driver, AsyncDriver, the ten Supports* and async mirrors, DriverBackend, AsyncDriverBackend, Entry, Page, PutResult, WriteHandle, Op)?

options.label: New remote_store.drivers module (Recommended)
options.description: One public namespace for authors, both runtimes in it; added to check_api_docs' _PUBLIC_NAMESPACES with index rows and one API page. MemoryDriver goes in remote_store.backends, AsyncMemoryDriver in remote_store.aio. Store users' namespaces stay unchanged.

options.label: Split: sync in remote_store, async in remote_store.aio
options.description: Mirrors how Backend/AsyncBackend are exported today. Each name joins an existing __all__, so the top-level namespace grows by about 20 author-only names.

options.label: remote_store.backends / remote_store.aio.backends
options.description: Next to the concrete backends. Short import, but mixes author protocols with user-facing backend classes in one listing.

questions.question: Rule 13 must be restated over the driver's probe for kernel classes. How does the test find a kernel class's driver class?

options.label: Test-side map, fails closed (Recommended)
options.description: test_health_probe_declared keeps _DRIVERS = {MemoryBackend: MemoryDriver, ...}; a discovered kernel class not in it fails. The probe owner is resolved in the driver's MRO against the Driver/AsyncDriver Protocol defaults. Memory's drivers omit probe and inherit the Protocol no-op, so the PING-008 exemption holds. No new public attribute.

options.label: ClassVar on each kernel class
options.description: Public classes declare driver_class: ClassVar[type]; the test reads it. Self-describing, but adds a public attribute every future backend must set, which the guide then has to teach.

questions.question: Which RFC-0021 stances go into the new narrow ADR (ADR-0047), accepted with ADR-0042?

options.label: D1, D2, D3, D4, D8 (Recommended)
options.description: All five carry rejected alternatives in RFC-0021 (lines 158-174), and D3/D4 are the stances a future driver author most needs: undecodable state is not in the store, and the library never writes one (BE-008's opt-in check retired). Points to BE-032 for the contract.

options.label: D1, D2, D8 only
options.description: The minimum the maintainer named. D3/D4 stay recorded only in the RFC and BE-032; shorter ADR, but the BE-008 retirement has no ADR behind it.

questions.question: BackendContract.dfy's DeleteFolder requires a recursive delete to empty the subtree, which a kernel walk over a stored non-canonical key (Path is any non-empty string) does not. How should the model be reconciled?

options.label: Guard the ensures (Recommended)
options.description: Add a predicate that every key under path is canonical, and guard the recursive success and emptiness postconditions with it; otherwise the trait allows DirectoryNotEmpty. Both MemoryBackend.dfy refinements must still verify (Docker Dafny). The encoding wiring itself stays with BK-434.

options.label: Precondition on DeleteFolder
options.description: requires canonical subtree. Simpler, but a precondition makes the state unreachable for callers rather than stating the kernel's answer, and the oracle can no longer be driven into it.

options.label: Re-home to BK-434
options.description: Leave the model as is, and move the two 'reconciling is BK-394's' sentences in BE-030/BE-031 to BK-434. Smallest PR, but the model knowingly disagrees with the first accepted class.
